units.translation: 306. Greedily: he ate voraciously, having pleasure equal to a dream, not even now believing that he is feasting because of what he has suffered, but thinking it to be like a dream.
308. To be awake means to be wakeful; and 'they remained' instead of 'they awaited'. P
310. Limits: what they must cross. And 'accomplishment'—he used this word wittily and aptly; for 'to accomplish' properly means to do something with toil, as we say even to this day.
311-12a. Hear now: 'now' is used for 'therefore'. Through 'therefore' he renders the prophecy as if owed to them, saying: 'Listen therefore, as if receiving what is due'.

b. 〈Not all things:〉 He says this so that they may not trouble him later by seeking exactness. And he divinely attributes the cause of this to the gods and not to himself, saying: 'But whatever has arisen dear to the gods I will not conceal'.
c. Has arisen: instead of 'exists'. Lg (P)
313. 'I was infatuated' is used for 'I grieved'. He calls 'folly' the lack of counsel. And he adds the reason why he grieved Zeus. P

314. Prophesying in order: prophesying to all in sequence and completely. He sets forth his own misfortunes, already making clear that he does not prophesy to them accurately or perfectly, since he was harmed for this reason.
315-16a. Deficient: not perfect, but still lacking something in the oracles revealed to men, so that they may have need of the divine.
c. 'Oracles of prophecy' means the decrees of the prophetic art. P

317-18a. The rocks: concerning the Symplegades, that they were at the mouth of the Pontus and that they were called Cyaneae because of their color, has been said in Book 1 (v. 2 sq.). He terrifies the heroes through everything and from the first hearing, both through the ebb and flow of the rocks and through the narrow strait in the sea, which even on land is exceedingly dangerous and fearful. L
b. In the straits of the sea: where the sea narrows. He speaks of the mouth of the Pontus. Lg (P)
319. Completely escape: he says this because no one ever escaped completely unharmed, so not even the Argo, despite Hera's forethought.
320a. 'To be fixed' means 'to be strong'. P
b. Lowest: those that are in the depths. Lg (P)

321. But often they come together: he heightens the dread of the speech through everything, both through their not simply coming together but continuously, and through their being opposite. For if they came together from the sides, perhaps it would somehow be possible to escape by observing the meeting; but if they come together from opposite directions, the danger is direct and acknowledged. He also makes it terrible and strikes the heroes with the hearing, since he received great benefits from them, so that he himself, foretelling great and terrible things, may appear as an equal benefactor.
